question: Operating characteristics of each stopping rule applied to the SAME fixed, role-ordered ladder
why_literature_does_not_settle_it: Matuschek et al. (2017) cover one simple crossed design and data-driven order; Barr et al. (2013) and Seedorff et al. (2019) differ in rules; no published test of back-off on singular/non-convergent fits as a rule (searches found none); Sim 1 here covers one small design only
factors_and_levels: Design D1 crossed subj x item 2-level factor; D2 crossed 2x2 within (focal interaction); subjects {12,24,48,96}; items {8,16,32,64}; slope SD/residual SD {0,.1,.2,.4,.8}; RE correlation {0,.5,.9}; MCAR missing {0,.1,.3}; coding {deviation, treatment}
methods_compared: maximal (no reduction); back-off on non-convergence only; back-off on singular-or-nonconvergent (unprotected); protected back-off (focal slopes kept); LRT alpha {.05,.1,.2} naive chi2 and chi-bar-square; AIC; BIC; rePCA threshold rule (Bates et al. 2015); CRI/cs substitution (Scandola & Tidoni 2024)
performance_measures: Type I error, power, CI coverage, bias/RMSE of focal beta, rung distribution, convergence and singular rates, runtime
reps_and_MCSE: 2,000 reps per H0 cell (MCSE about 0.5 points at .05); 1,000 per H1 cell; fractional factorial (e.g. Latin hypercube over size x tau x rho) with metamodel
rough_cost: Gaussian: about 0.07 s per lmer fit at 384 rows (measured here, lme4 1.1-35.1); about 8 fits per rep; core grid of about 200 cells: roughly 200 CPU-hours

question: Does the ORDER of droppable terms matter (role-first, J_eff-first, data-driven smallest-variance-first)?
why_literature_does_not_settle_it: Bates et al. (2015) and afex use data-driven order; Verissimo (2023) and Heisig et al. (2017) suggest correlated or compositionally heterogeneous nuisance slopes matter; Luo & Li (2023) say level-1 slopes are not essential for level-2 focal effects (conflict)
factors_and_levels: D3 crossed or nested with nuisance covariate x2 correlated with focal x1 within units r {0,.3,.6}; nuisance slope SD {0,.2,.4}; compositional heterogeneity of x2 (predictor ICC {0,.2,.5}); focal effect level {within, between, cross-level}
performance_measures: Type I error and power for focal effect; SE calibration (mean SE / empirical SD)

question: Which singularity / convergence criterion should the registry use, and how scale-dependent is it?
why_literature_does_not_settle_it: lme4 theta < 1e-4 depends on predictor units (catalogue L4-04); glmmTMB cannot reach the boundary; statsmodels uses an absolute 0.01 threshold; no literature on rule-level consequences
factors_and_levels: predictor scaling {x, 10x, x/10}; tolerance {1e-3,1e-4,1e-6} on relative eigenvalues; engines {lme4 2.x, glmmTMB 1.1.15.x, statsmodels 0.15}; true tau near 0
performance_measures: agreement of rung reached across engines and scalings; downstream Type I error

question: Is non-convergence evidence of over-parameterisation in GLMMs with current engines?
why_literature_does_not_settle_it: Bates et al. (2015) say non-convergence usually means too complex; Eager & Roy (2017) found 82% non-convergence in complex logistic models with known non-zero variances (old lme4)
factors_and_levels: Bernoulli logit (base rate {.5,.2,.05}), Poisson (mean {1,5}); cluster size {5,20}; J {10,30,100}; true slope SD {0,.3,.6}; Laplace vs nAGQ (where allowed); engines lme4 2.x and glmmTMB
methods_compared: back-off on non-convergence vs on singular vs LRT .2 vs protected; with and without multi-optimiser re-check (allFit-like)
performance_measures: false back-off rate (backing off when true variance > 0), Type I error, power, coverage
rough_cost: GLMM fits about 10x slower: roughly 400 CPU-hours for a 100-cell grid

question: Few-cluster education designs: cross-level interactions and level-2 effects
why_literature_does_not_settle_it: Heisig & Schaeffer (2019) and Luo & Li (2023) support the lower-level slope; Huang & Zhang (2025) offer RI + CR2; Zhang & Lai (2024) found KR with random slopes miscalibrated under level-2 heteroscedasticity; Oberpriller et al. (2022) back off to fixed grouping on singular fits
factors_and_levels: pupils in classes (in schools); J {6,10,20,40}; cluster size {10,25}; cluster-size CV {0,.5}; slope SD {0,.15,.3}; level-2 heteroscedasticity {none, moderate}; CRT randomised at class
methods_compared: protected ladder with Satterthwaite / KR; RI + CR2; fixed-effects grouping fallback; REML + t(df) per Elff et al. (2021)
performance_measures: Type I error, power, coverage for cross-level and level-2 effects

question: Calibration of outcome-blind design analysis (L1-18): does a pre-fit simulated probability of singular fit / of reaching each rung predict what happens?
why_literature_does_not_settle_it: No literature found; the feature is new
factors_and_levels: assumed theta vs true theta mismatch {exact, 0.5x, 2x}; designs D1, D4
performance_measures: calibration (Brier score, reliability curve) of predicted rung probabilities

question: Post-selection inference and reporting: how far do selected-rung results differ from ceiling/protected results, and does showing both change decisions?
why_literature_does_not_settle_it: Bates et al. (2015) found no change in three data sets; no systematic evidence
methods_compared: selected rung vs ceiling vs protected rung
performance_measures: decision disagreement rate; coverage conditional on rung

question: Engine dependence of the rung reached (parity)
why_literature_does_not_settle_it: No literature; engines differ in warnings and boundary handling
factors_and_levels: H1 subset; engines lme4, glmmTMB, statsmodels (one grouping factor or variance components), optional Rust engines
methods_compared: same rule with registry criteria evaluated by the suite
performance_measures: rung agreement, focal-estimate agreement under one reference objective

question: Masked (blinded) ladder execution
why_literature_does_not_settle_it: Sim 5 shows exact invariance for Gaussian LMMs up to optimiser tolerance; GLMMs untested
factors_and_levels: GLMM families as H4; masking by offset on the linear predictor vs label-preserving residual masking
performance_measures: rung agreement; Type I error after masked selection

question: Frequentist calibration of terminal alternatives (penalised/MAP, Bayesian with declared priors, model averaging)
why_literature_does_not_settle_it: Chung et al. (2013) and Oberauer (2022) address estimation or Bayes factors, not frequentist error of the full procedure; Heck & Bockting and Martinez-Huertas & Olmos (2022) target model recovery or variance recovery
factors_and_levels: H1 small-sample cells where the protected rung fails; priors {weakly informative half-normal / LKJ(2)}
methods_compared: blme MAP; brms/Stan full Bayes; Akaike-weight averaging
performance_measures: Type I error/coverage of focal effect; runtime
rough_cost: MCMC: roughly 60 s per fit, about 200 CPU-hours for 20 cells
